t: You're on St James's Street, the principal road of the St James's district. It runs from Piccadilly down to Pall Mall and St James's Palace, whose main gatehouse stands at the southern end. In the seventeenth century, Clarendon House faced down this street across Piccadilly. One person connected to the street is Edward Harbord, the third Baron Suffield, a British politician and abolitionist, who died here in 1835. So a campaigner against slavery spent his final days on this very street.
